_comment_h6: Bug-1 canonical reproducer — UNDER-SUBSCRIBED variant. Same shared cgroup constraint (cpu.max=10000 100000 = 10% of one CPU) as `bug1_canonical.json`, but configured for the LIVE workload band (~0.13 tasks/cpu — paired with `--cpus 32` produces 4 tasks / 32 cpus = 0.125 tasks/cpu, well inside the 0.13–0.57 live band identified by `investigate-dsq-insert-vs-vtime-path-divergence`). The canonical fixture is over-subscribed at 4.0 tasks/cpu (16 tasks / 4 cpus) which biases LAVD's dispatch path toward `dsq_insert_vtime` — under-sub flips that toward simple `dsq_insert` via the wakeup → select_cpu → can_direct_dispatch chain. cpu.max constraint is identical so cgroup_bw library is exercised the same way; only the workload axis changes. See tg `bug1-canonical-fixture-add-undersub-variant`.
_comment_run_units: rt-app units: `run` and `sleep` are microseconds. 50000us run + 50000us sleep = 50ms run + 50ms sleep cycle (50% duty cycle per task, oscillating). 4 tasks × 50% = 2.0 CPUs of aggregate demand; with `--cpus 32` available, NO CPU-side contention exists — the cgroup's 10ms-per-100ms quota is the SOLE binding constraint. This isolates whether cpu-bw-stall-bug requires CPU oversubscription to reproduce.
